description:
📐 **POSITION KOINE AGAINST A PUBLISHED GOVERNANCE TAXONOMY — decide scope, do not reflexively specify.** [Kang & Diponegoro, *Governance Gaps in Agent Interoperability Protocols*, arXiv 2606.31498, 30 June 2026](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.31498) analyses MCP, A2A, ACP, ANP and ERC-8004 against six dimensions — **membership, deliberation, voting, dissent preservation, human escalation, audit/replay** — and concludes that *"agent community governance constitutes a missing architectural layer above current interoperability standards, not a missing feature within them."*

**That is koine's own structural thesis, independently reached, and it is the strongest external evidence the project has.** Their dimensions barely intersect koine's (license propagation, egress control, trust tiers, budget ceilings, capability grants), so there is **no prior-art threat** — this is validation, and the specs should cite it.

**The inverse is the real question, and it is a SCOPE question rather than a work item.** Measured 2026-08-13 against `specs/`:

| Their dimension | koine today |
|---|---|
| membership | partly — `identity.md` (KINP) |
| audit | partly — `capability-bus.md`, `fine-tuning.md`, `media-interchange.md` |
| replay | partly — `conformance-scenario.md` (KCS) |
| **deliberation** | **absent** |
| **voting** | **absent** |
| **dissent preservation** | **absent** |

**Do NOT assume the three absences are gaps.** Two facts argue they are not koine's: (1) cuneiform already implements voting as an **orchestration strategy** (`workforce/orchestrator.rs` — pipeline/star/hierarchy/voting over one ASSEMBLED org), which is agents inside a single organization deciding a task, not two organizations deliberating; and (2) **no cross-org edge in the tree needs a vote** — `talos → argos` is analysis, `insimul → lugh` is training, the rest are capability invocations and data flows. koine exists for INTER-organizational interop, so a dimension exercised only within one org belongs to cuneiform.

Note also that the paper offers a **taxonomy, not a specification**, so there is nothing to adopt by reference. Specifying these would mean koine INVENTING three protocol dimensions — the opposite of the direction `78-kft-adopt-by-reference` and `73`/`74` just established. **A stated non-goal is worth as much as a spec**, and it is this repo's own discipline: no gate fires on a value nobody wrote.

userStories.title: Cite the paper where it validates the layer claim
userStories.description: External, independent confirmation that the layer koine occupies is real and missing is worth more than any internal argument, and the specs currently assert it unaided.
acceptanceCriteria: The paper is cited in the spec(s) that assert koine sits ABOVE MCP/A2A rather than competing with them, with its conclusion quoted accurately and its scope stated — it analyses five protocols against six governance dimensions, which is a different axis from koine's license/egress/tier/budget/grant dimensions.
The citation makes the NON-overlap explicit, so a reader cannot mistake validation for prior art over koine's own claims.
It is pinned by arXiv id and date, not by title alone — this repo's own upstream-pins discipline (`76`).

userStories.title: Map all six against the specs, and record where coverage is partial
userStories.description: Three dimensions are already partly covered. 'Partly' is the answer that needs writing down, because it is the one a reader will otherwise re-derive.
acceptanceCriteria: For membership, audit and replay: name WHICH spec covers it, WHAT it covers, and what it does NOT — e.g. whether KCS replay is scenario replay or decision replay, which are different claims.
Where coverage is partial and the shortfall matters, it becomes a named finding rather than prose — the `72-kgp-findings-closure` posture.
The mapping lives where a future scan will find it, so this question is answered once.

userStories.title: Decide deliberation, voting and dissent — in or out, with a re-open trigger
userStories.description: The load-bearing story. A NON-GOAL is a valid and probably correct outcome; what is not valid is leaving three named dimensions unaddressed after a published taxonomy has named them.
acceptanceCriteria: Each of the three gets an explicit verdict — IN SCOPE (and therefore a spec change) or NON-GOAL (and therefore a stated boundary) — with the reason recorded.

The evidence for a non-goal is the one measured here: cuneiform implements voting as an intra-org orchestration strategy, and no cross-organizational edge in the tree requires a collective decision. If that stops being true, the verdict changes — so state the TRIGGER that re-opens it (a cross-org use case requiring two organizations to reach a joint decision).

If any is IN SCOPE, it is scoped as a PROFILE over an existing standard wherever one exists, never as an invention — the `78-kft-adopt-by-reference` rule. If no standard exists, that absence is recorded as part of the justification.
The decision is a `decisions/` record, so it is citable and closes the question rather than being re-asked at every portfolio scan.
